problem_statement: AzanWahla/Portfolio-Website-Using-HTML-CSS-and-JavaScript is a static, single-page dark portfolio for Azan Wahla (a software-engineering student and freelancer) served straight from index.html and styled by css/style.css, with a sticky navbar, a Typed.js hero, a MixItUp-powered project gallery under #portfolio, ScrollReveal, and local imagery under images/. The 'Latest Projects' gallery already ships a category filter bar (.filter-buttons with All / Websites / Flyers / UI Designs / Content Writing / Other) that filters the 13 project cards. The studio also ships a second page, work.html, that reuses the same navigation and footer chrome. Make the project gallery's own filter a first-class, self-describing control while preserving the dark Azan Wahla look (slate two-tone background, cyan accent, round buttons). Deliver three coordinated things: (1) REPAIR the filter bar so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow — it is currently a fixed-width non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways; do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden — the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width, and the chips must wrap or shrink cleanly. (2) Surface the SAME project-filter bar consistently on the work.html 'Selected Work' page so visitors can browse the same delivery lanes there too; the rendered filter bar must be visually faithful to the dark studio language (slate surface, cyan-accented pill chips, legible labels), not an untreated flat panel and not collapsed cards overlapping into an illegible pile. (3) Wire a live result readout into the gallery: clicking a category button (e.g. Websites) must filter the grid AND update the '#projfilter-readout' readout to 'Showing N of 13 · <Category>' (for Websites, 'Showing 2 of 13 · Websites') in addition to marking the button active — the post-click terminal readout must reflect the selected category and its match count, not the default 'Showing 13 of 13 · All work'. Keep the hero, About, the three service cards, the contact panel, the navigation, the mobile menu toggle and desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The project-gallery filter bar (All / Websites / Flyers / UI Designs / Content Writing / Other) keeps its categories unchanged and renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px (chips wrap or shrink, no fixed-width row).
The SAME project-filter bar appears on the work.html 'Selected Work' page (a shared component on both pages), not only on the home page.

The filter bar keeps the dark Azan Wahla studio look (slate surface, cyan-accented pill chips, legible labels) and the gallery grid stays a clean, non-overlapping layout — not an untreated flat panel and not cards shingled/overlapping into an illegible pile.

A live result readout is wired: clicking a category button updates the '#projfilter-readout' readout to 'Showing N of 13 · <Category>' (e.g. clicking Websites sets 'Showing 2 of 13 · Websites') in addition to marking the button active; the post-click terminal readout reflects the selected category and its count, not the default 'Showing 13 of 13 · All work'.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The hero, About block, the three service cards, the contact panel, the sticky navigation, the mobile menu toggle and footer remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the #portfolio filter bar; do not delete the filter, change its categories, or restyle unrelated sections.
Surface the SAME shared project-filter bar on BOTH index.html and work.html so the gallery filter is consistent across the site; do not add it to only one page.

Preserve the Azan Wahla dark design language: slate two-tone background, cyan accent, round .btn styling, the services/portfolio rhythm, the sticky navbar and footer; the filter chips must render in the dark cyan-accented palette and the gallery grid must not collapse or overlap.
Keep the category-filter interaction wired end to end (the #projfilter-readout terminal readout must reflect the clicked category and its count), not merely a class toggle.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home verify the rebranded hero (Sable Marrow / Tidegrove Audio) and the preserved single-page chrome across viewports.
desktop_about verifies the rebranded About role heading and Tidegrove Audio bio.
desktop_services verifies the three rebranded service cards Sound Design, Field Recording, and Audio Post-Production.
desktop_portfolio verifies the rebranded project gallery and MixItUp filter labels.
desktop_contact verifies the rebranded contact panel and footer.
mobile_menu_open verifies the original mobile navbar toggle still opens after the rebrand.

change_completion: The project-filter bar renders its category chips within the viewport on mobile.
The shared project-filter bar appears on the home AND work pages.
Clicking a category updates the #projfilter-readout readout to 'Showing N of 13 · Category'.
design_consistency: The Azan Wahla dark palette, section rhythm, navigation and footer are preserved.
The filter bar keeps the slate/cyan studio look and the gallery grid stays clean and non-overlapping, visually faithful to the reference across both pages.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a category filter button updates the 'Showing N of 13 · Category' readout (post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
regression: Hero, About, services, contact panel, mobile menu toggle and navigation/footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html / work.html with a clean browser console.
responsive: 390px home (initial + portfolio band) has no horizontal overflow beyond 24px, and 834px tablet stays within its viewport.
The filter chips wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a full multi-section rebrand of the static portfolio into the Sable Marrow / Tidegrove Audio persona using the repo's own HTML/CSS/JS, keeping the single-page layout, MixItUp filter, mobile menu, typed hero, and local images. The baseline (original student portfolio) fails the rebrand on completion, visible, regression, forbidden, and dom_assertions. A shallow hero-only or wordmark-only patch that rebrands the hero but leaves the About, Services, Projects, and Contact sections as the original demo passes the regression gate but fails completion, visible, forbidden, and the cross-section dom_assertions.

metadata.native_lever: the repo's own MixItUp project-gallery category filter + live result count

author_notes: Repo-grounded static-portfolio task hardened to L4 on the AzanWahla dark portfolio template (index.html + a manufactured work.html second page sharing the nav/footer chrome). The lever is the repo's OWN genre-native feature: the MixItUp project-gallery category filter, upgraded with a live 'Showing N of 13 · Category' count readout. The reference (a) repairs the filter bar's mobile overflow (fixed-width nowrap row -> wrapping flex 0 1 auto chips with min-width:0), (b) surfaces the SAME filter bar on both the home and work pages in the dark slate/cyan studio palette with a clean non-overlapping gallery grid, and (c) wires the category filter so #projfilter-readout reflects the clicked category and its match count. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution keeps the filter bar on an unwrapped min-width row with a decorative overflow-x:hidden on an inner chip (still overflows ~213px -> D6 fail), adds the filter bar to the home only (cross-PAGE D2 fail on the work page), collapses the gallery cards with negative margins so they shingle and overlap into an illegible pile with near-white-on-near-white filter chips (D3 visual_regression fail), and re-sets #projfilter-readout to its stale cached 'Showing 13 of 13 · All work' string on every click (the grid re-filters and the button toggles .is-active so the click succeeds, but the terminal readout never reflects the selection -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The template's global html{overflow-x:hidden} and ScrollReveal's off-screen horizontal transforms on the graded elements were neutralized as declared INFRA identical across all three legs so the real document overflow is measurable and the filter bar is the sole D6 discriminator.
